CONFIDENTIAL
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
S.I. Special Branch
REPORT
Date Oct. 8, 1939
Subject. Rodolfo Brandt - Mexican
Made by. J.S.L. MacAdie Forwarded by. C. [Signature]

Rodolfo Brandt, a Mexican citizen, came to
Shanghai for the first time, it is believed, just
prior to the 1937 hostilities and took up residence
in the Broadway Mansions. At that time he remarked
that his father was a banker and that he himself was
on a tour. He had no apparent employment but on
the outbreak of hostilities he evacuated Broadway
Mansions and moved to the Metropole Hotel where
almost immediately he commenced working for John
Morriss of United Press, taking press photographs
and covering war news. He continued in this
capacity and went all over China to the various
fronts and towns in the Chinese rear. In February,
1938, he was dismissed from the United Press on
account of his being heavily in debt in Shanghai
and he then left for Singapore where he is stated
to have obtained a position in the Straits Times.
In August, 1938, he was in Manila believed unemployed
and on August 25 the Commissioner of Police received
a letter from the Mexican Consulate enquiring as to
Brandt's whereabouts.

In 1939 he was back in Shanghai again
and was working for W. Koreska & Co., Stationers,
132 Yuen Ming Yuen Road, in what capacity, is not
known. This firm is Viennese but has been
established in Shanghai for a few years and is not
a Jewish "emigrant" firm.

（左侧批注：H FILE / yr.）

机密
上海公共租界工部局警务处。
特别情报科（S.I. Special Branch）
报告
日期：1939年10月8日
事由：罗多尔福·布兰特（Rodolfo Brandt）——墨西哥人
制作人：J.S.L. 麦卡迪（MacAdie） 转呈人：C. [签名]

罗多尔福·布兰特，墨西哥公民，据信于1937年战事爆发前夕首次来到上海，并入住百老汇大厦（Broadway Mansions）。当时他声称其父为银行家，而他本人正在游历。他表面上没有职业，但在战事爆发后，他搬离百老汇大厦，迁至大都会酒店（Metropole Hotel），几乎立即开始为合众社（United Press）的约翰·莫里斯（John Morriss）工作，拍摄新闻照片并报道战地新闻。他以此身份继续工作，足迹遍布中国各前线及大后方城镇。1938年2月，因在上海负债累累，他被合众社解雇，随后前往新加坡，据称在《海峡时报》（Straits Times）谋得职位。1938年8月，他在马尼拉，据信处于失业状态；8月25日，警务处处长收到墨西哥领事馆来信，查询布兰特的下落。

1939年，他再次回到上海，受雇于圆明园路132号的文具商 W. Koreska & Co.，具体职务不详。该公司虽为维也纳背景，但已在上海设立数年，并非犹太“移民”公司。

（左侧批注：H 档案 / 年份）

At the end of July, Brandt again moved into
the Broadway Mansions, occupying Room 531. While at
this address, he applied to the management for
permission to erect a large aerial on the roof for
use with a radio transmitter which he would instal
in his room. He was informed that if he obtained
permission in writing not only from the Japanese
Military but also from the Naval Landing Party and
the Japanese Consular Police, the management would
be quite willing to agree. Brandt asserted that he
would have no difficulty in obtaining permission from
all three organs as he had considerable influence with
Japanese officials. However he never produced the
requisite documents and towards the end of September,
he left Broadway Mansions ostensibly to reside in
French Town. Actually he sailed with his wife Mrs.
T.O. Brandt on the s.s."Conte Biancamano" to Hongkong
on September 24, Mrs. Brandt going on to Manila.

The only record against Brandt in Police files
is a complaint made by Elly Widler (Swiss) (Vide File
D.4231) on September 3, 1937 to the effect that Brandt
had suggested that he, Widler was responsible for the
theft of a valuable camera, which had been taken from
Brandt's room by friends as a practical joke.

Brandt is of German origin.
                                        R.W. Mac Culloch
                                            D.S.I.

D.C. (Special Branch)

7月底，布兰特再次搬入百老汇大厦，入住531室。在此期间，他向管理处申请许可，拟在屋顶架设大型天线，供其安装在房间内的无线电发射机使用。管理处告知他，如果他能获得日本军方、日本海军陆战队以及日本领事警察三方的书面许可，管理处将乐意同意。布兰特声称，由于他与日本官员关系深厚，获得这三方机构的许可毫无困难。然而，他从未出示所需文件，并于9月下旬离开百老汇大厦， ostensibly（表面上）声称要迁居法租界。实际上，他与妻子 T.O. 布兰特夫人于9月24日乘坐“比安卡马诺伯爵号”（s.s. "Conte Biancamano"）轮船前往香港，布兰特夫人则继续前往马尼拉。

警方档案中关于布兰特的唯一记录是瑞士人艾莉·维德勒（Elly Widler）于1937年9月3日提出的投诉（参见档案 D.4231），大意是布兰特暗示维德勒对其贵重相机失窃一事负责，而该相机实则是被朋友作为恶作剧从布兰特房间拿走。

布兰特系德裔出身。
                                        R.W. 麦卡洛克（Mac Culloch）
                                            特别情报科副督察（D.S.I.）

刑事侦缉处（特别科）主管

1.

Complaint of Mr. Fidler (Swiss) Broadway
Mansions against Mr. R. Brandt (Mexican).

At 10 a.m. Sept. 3, 1937 Mr. Elly Widler (Swiss)
came to Central Station and made a complaint as
follows:-

About one month ago he made the acquaintance of a
Mr. R. Brandt (Mexican) residing Room 502, Metropol Hotel,
and employed with the United Press as photographer.

At about 8 a.m. Sept. 2, 1937 Mr. Widler visited Mr.
Brandt concerning a previous matter which was settled
amicably.

After Mr. Widler left, Mr. Brandt made a complaint
to the manager of the Metropol that a valuable camera
was missing from his room and mentioned the visit of Mr.
Widler. The manager suggested that the house keeper
make enquiries and the Police be informed if the camera
was not found.

At about 10.30 a.m. same day Mr. Brandt informed
the reception clerk Mr. W. F. Scheeva in the presence of
a porter named Mr. R. Oppenheim that the camera was
returned and that Mr. Widler had played a joke on him.

Mr. Widler was visiting the Metropol Hotel again
at 11 a.m. same day when he was accosted by the manager
to whom Mr. Widler denied all knowledge of the matter.
Mr. Widler was able to see Mr. Brandt at 5 p.m. same

菲德勒先生（瑞士籍，百老汇大厦）对 R. 布兰特先生（墨西哥籍）的投诉。

1937年9月3日上午10时，瑞士人艾莉·维德勒（Elly Widler）来到中央分局并提出如下投诉：

约一个月前，他结识了居住在大都会酒店502室、受雇于合众社担任摄影师的 R. 布兰特先生（墨西哥籍）。

1937年9月2日上午8时许，维德勒先生就先前已友好解决的事项拜访了布兰特先生。

维德勒先生离开后，布兰特先生向大都会酒店经理投诉，称其房间内丢失了一台贵重相机，并提到了维德勒先生的来访。经理建议由管家进行调查，若未找到相机则通知警方。

同日上午10时30分左右，布兰特先生在一名名为 R. 奥本海姆（R. Oppenheim）的服务员在场的情况下，告知接待员 W. F. 谢瓦（W. F. Scheeva）先生，相机已归还，且维德勒先生只是跟他开了个玩笑。

同日中午11时，维德勒先生再次造访大都会酒店时，被经理拦住询问，维德勒先生否认对此事有任何了解。同日下午5时，维德勒先生得以见到布兰特先生
